hints.content: As $x$ approaches positive infinity, what value does $f(x)$ seem to approach on each of the graphs?
Only on graph A does $f(x)$ seem to approach $3$ as $x$ approaches positive infinity.

question.content:
Consider graphs A, B, and C. The dashed lines represent asymptotes.

**Which graphs agree with this statement?**

$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to \infty}f(x)=3$

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: In this graph, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to \infty}f(x)$ indeed seems to approach $3$.

The first curve moves downward away from a horizontal asymptote at y = 3, then toward a vertical asymptote at x = 3. The second curve moves downward away from the vertical asymptote at x = 3, then toward the horizontal asymptote at y = 3.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/cd8844406b8f66bef3b7613b09566959c66b18bd)
